arxiv-1908-01841.title: DLGNet: A Transformer-based Model for Dialogue Response Generation
arxiv-1908-01841.creator: Oluwatobi O. Olabiyi, Erik T. Mueller
arxiv-1908-01841.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Oluwatobi O. Olabiyi, Erik T. Mueller. Neural dialogue models, despite their successes, still suffer from lack of relevance, diversity, and in many cases coherence in their generated responses. These issues can attributed to reasons including (1) short-range model architectures that capture limited temporal dependencies, (2) limitations of the maximum likelihood training objective, (3) the concave entropy profile of dialogue datasets resulting in short and generic responses, and (4) the out-of-vocabulary problem leading to generation of a large number of < < UNK > >

arxiv-2012-06030.title: A family of concordance homomorphisms from Khovanov homology
arxiv-2012-06030.creator: William Ballinger
arxiv-2012-06030.description: Abstract . By considering a version of Khovanov homology incorporating both the Lee and E ⁡ ( − 1 ) E(-1) differentials, we construct a 1 1 -parameter family of concordance homomorphisms similar to the Upsilon invariant from knot Floer homology.

arxiv-2110-05779.title: Synthesizing quasi-bound states in the continuum in epsilon-near-zero layered materials
arxiv-2110-05779.creator: Giuseppe Castaldi, Massimo Moccia, Vincenzo Galdi
arxiv-2110-05779.description: Abstract Bound states in the continuum (BIC) are highly confined, nonradiative modes that can exist in open structures, despite their potential compatibility and coupling with the radiation spectrum, and may give rise to resonances with arbitrarily large lifetimes. Here, we study this phenomenon in layered materials featuring epsilon-near-zero constituents.

arxiv-2311-13937.title: Exploring Methods for Cross-lingual Text Style Transfer: The Case of Text Detoxification
arxiv-2311-13937.creator: Daryna Dementieva, Daniil Moskovskiy, David Dale and Alexander Panchenko
arxiv-2311-13937.description: Abstract Text detoxification is the task of transferring the style of text from toxic to neutral. While there are approaches yielding promising results in monolingual setup, e.g., Dale et al. 2021 ; Hallinan et al. 2022 , cross-lingual transfer for this task remains a challenging open problem Moskovskiy et al. 2022 .

arxiv-2404-11552.title: Simultaneous Estimation of Piecewise Constant Coefficients in Elliptic PDEs via Bayesian Level-Set Methods
arxiv-2404-11552.creator: Anuj Abhishek a and Thilo Strauss b and Taufiquar Khan c
arxiv-2404-11552.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Anuj Abhishek a and Thilo Strauss b and Taufiquar Khan c. In this article, we propose a non-parametric Bayesian level-set method for simultaneous reconstruction of two different piecewise constant coefficients in an elliptic partial differential equation. We show that the Bayesian formulation of the corresponding inverse problem is well-posed and that the posterior measure as a solution to the inverse problem satisfies a Lipschitz estimate with respect to the measured data in terms of Hellinger distance.

arxiv-2410-01558.title: Nonlinear Scattering Theory for Asymptotically de Sitter Vacuum Solutions in All Even Spatial Dimensions
arxiv-2410-01558.creator: Serban Cicortas
arxiv-2410-01558.description: Abstract The purpose of this paper is to establish a definitive quantitative nonlinear scattering theory for asymptotically de Sitter solutions of the Einstein vacuum equations in ( n + 1 ) (n+1) dimensions with n ≥ 4 n\geq 4 even, which are determined by small scattering data at the spacelike asymptotic boundaries ℐ − \mathcal{I}^{-} and ℐ + . \mathcal{I}^{+}.

arxiv-2412-14253.title: From the EFT to the UV: the complete SMEFT one-loop dictionary
arxiv-2412-14253.creator: Guilherme Guedes, Pablo Olgoso
arxiv-2412-14253.description: Abstract Effective field theories (EFTs) provide an excellent framework for the search of heavy physics beyond the Standard Model, using the so-called bottom-up and top-down approaches. However, the vastness of possible UV scenarios makes the complete connection between the two approaches a difficult challenge at the loop-level. UV/IR dictionaries fill precisely this gap, efficiently connecting the EFT with the UV.

arxiv-2508-13911.title: PhysGM: Large Physical Gaussian Model for Feed-Forward 4D Synthesis
arxiv-2508-13911.creator: Chunji Lv, Zequn Chen, Donglin Di, Weinan Zhang, Hao Li, Wei Chen, Changsheng Li
arxiv-2508-13911.description: Abstract While physics-grounded 3D motion synthesis has seen significant progress, current methods face critical limitations. They typically rely on pre-reconstructed 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representations, while physics integration depends on either inflexible, manually defined physical attributes or unstable, optimization-heavy guidance from video models.

arxiv-2512-12085.title: Kardar-Parisi-Zhang and glassy properties in 2D Anderson localization: eigenstates and wave packets
arxiv-2512-12085.creator: Noam Izem, Bertrand Georgeot, Jiangbin Gong, Gabriel Lemarié, Sen Mu
arxiv-2512-12085.description: Abstract Despite decades of research, the universal nature of fluctuations in disordered quantum systems remains poorly understood. Here, we present extensive numerical evidence that fluctuations in two-dimensional (2D) Anderson localization belongs to the ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) -dimensional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) universality class.

pmc-10531399.title: The Contribution of Lipidomics in Ovarian Cancer Management: A Systematic Review
pmc-10531399.creator: Vasiliki Tzelepi, Helen Gika, Olga Begou, Eleni Timotheadou, Kentaro Nakayama
pmc-10531399.description: Lipidomics is a comprehensive study of all lipid components in living cells, serum, plasma, or tissues, with the aim of discovering diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive biomarkers for diseases such as malignant tumors. This systematic review evaluates studies, applying lipidomics to the diagnosis, prognosis, prediction, and differentiation of malignant and benign ovarian tumors.

pmc-10749970.title: The determinants of postpartum contraceptive use in Nigeria
pmc-10749970.creator: Obinna Princewill Anyatonwu, Kelechi Amy Nwoku, Håkan Jonsson, Fredinah Namatovu
pmc-10749970.description: IntroductionPostpartum contraception is vital for maternal and child health, and reduces the risk of infant mortality. The Health Belief Model (HBM) is a widely accepted framework for exploring health behaviors, such as contraceptive use. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the factors influencing postpartum contraceptive use in Nigeria and to contextualize the findings within the framework of the HBM.

pmc-11453494.title: 5074 Licorice Root Supplement As A Cause Of Hypokalemic Hypertension
pmc-11453494.creator: Gurbir Gill, Sherman Mitchell Harman, Lydia Alejandra Robles
pmc-11453494.description: Disclosure: G. Gill: None. S.M. Harman: None. L.A. Robles: None.A 67-year-old female Veteran presented to an emergency room with a one-day history of high blood pressure, chest tightness, and exertional dyspnea. Her blood pressure was 162/90 mm Hg, pulse regular at 71 BPM, and pain level 5/10.

pmc-11642393.title: Discovery of a Small Molecule with an Inhibitory Role for RAB11
pmc-11642393.creator: Camille Lempicki, Julian Milosavljevic, Christian Laggner, Simone Tealdi, Charlotte Meyer, Gerd Walz, Konrad Lang, Carlo Cosimo Campa, Tobias Hermle, George Mihai Nitulescu
pmc-11642393.description: RAB11, a pivotal RabGTPase, regulates essential cellular processes such as endocytic recycling, exocytosis, and autophagy. The protein was implicated in various human diseases, including cancer, neurodegenerative disorders, viral infections, and podocytopathies. However, a small-molecular inhibitor is lacking. The complexity and workload associated with potential assays make conducting large-scale screening for RAB11 challenging.

pmc-12749662.title: Tracing the tissue origin of cell-free DNA through open chromatin footprint
pmc-12749662.creator: Lingguo Li, Xiameizi Li, Yongjie Li, Fengxia Su, Yan Zhang, Zhuangyuan Tang, Jinghua Sun, Ya Gao, Xin Jin, Haiqiang Zhang
pmc-12749662.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a promising biomarker for liquid biopsy, essential for diagnosing and monitoring diseases. Current methods for estimating tissue contributions primarily rely on methylation markers, which can damage cfDNA, limiting clinical use. While research shows cfDNA coverage near transcription start sites (TSS) of actively transcribed genes decreases due to open chromatin, a comprehensive cross-tissue atlas has been lacking.

pmc-13124181.title: Validation of the Brazilian Version of the Cambridge Renal Stone Patient-Reported Outcome Measure (Br-CReSP) versus a Generic Questionnaire for Assessing Health-Related Quality of Life in Nephrolithiasis
pmc-13124181.creator: Alexandre Danilovic, Daniel Gabriele Sucupira, Oliver Wiseman, Elaine Brasil, Fabio Cesar Miranda Torricelli, Giovanni Scala Marchini, Carlos Batagello, Rodrigo Perrela, Fabio Carvalho Vicentini, William C. Nahas, Eduardo Mazzucchi
pmc-13124181.description: Purpose:No validated tool specifically assesses health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in Brazilian patients with kidney stones. The Cambridge Renal Stone Patient-Reported Outcome Measure (CReSP) is a self-administered questionnaire that evaluates the impact of kidney stones on patients’ QoL over the preceding seven days.

pmc-13424083.title: A federated blockchain framework for secure and intelligent smart farming in sustainable industrial agriculture
pmc-13424083.creator: Amar Y Jaffar
pmc-13424083.description: The fast growth of smart farming technologies and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors has transformed the agricultural sector, but has brought some fundamental problems, such as data privacy, scalability, and trust in distributed systems. In this paper, AgriChain-FL, a federated blockchain architecture, is introduced and guarantees privacy-preserving, transparent, and energy-efficient collaboration in agricultural ecosystems.

pmc-13589984.title: Dupilumab Improves Lung Function and Reduces Severe Exacerbations in Patients from China with Type 2 Asthma: A Subgroup Analysis of a Phase 3 Randomized Trial
pmc-13589984.creator: Qingling Zhang, Xiuhua Fu, Haohui Fang, Jie Lin, Arman Altincatal, Yvonne Huang, Jason H Kwah, Olivier Ledanois, Nanshan Zhong
pmc-13589984.description: PurposeAsthma affects approximately 46 million adults in China. The safety and efficacy of dupilumab, a monoclonal antibody which blocks the shared receptor component for interleukin (IL)-4 and IL-13, were evaluated in a phase 3 study in patients with moderate-to-severe asthma in the Asia–Pacific region (NCT03782532). This is a pre-specified subgroup analysis of patients in China derived from the Asia–Pacific trial.
